hints: Look first at the carbon carrying the OH group in X, Y and Z to decide if each alcohol is primary, secondary or tertiary.
Remember that primary and secondary alcohols are oxidised by mild oxidants like acidified dichromate, but tertiary alcohols resist oxidation.
Consider which dehydration product has the form RCH=CHR with two different groups on each C=C carbon, the condition needed for cis-trans isomerism.
walkthrough:
**Classify X, Y and Z**

X is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. The OH carbon has one alkyl group, so it is primary. Y is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. The OH carbon has two alkyl groups, so it is secondary. Z is $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{C(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. The OH carbon has three alkyl groups, so it is tertiary.

**Decide who reacts with mild oxidising agents**

Primary alcohols oxidise to aldehydes then carboxylic acids, secondary alcohols oxidise to ketones. Tertiary alcohols have no H on the C-OH carbon and resist mild oxidation.

$$\text{primary} \rightarrow \text{aldehyde} \rightarrow \text{acid, secondary} \rightarrow \text{ketone, tertiary} \rightarrow \text{no reaction}$$

**Conclude the oxidation column**

So X and Y only are oxidised. Z does not react. This already eliminates rows that include X, Y and Z.

**Examine dehydration to $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}$ alkenes**

X (pentan-1-ol) dehydrates mainly to pent-1-ene, $\text{CH}_2\text{=CHCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Y (pentan-3-ol) dehydrates to pent-2-ene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Z (2-methylbutan-2-ol) dehydrates mainly to 2-methylbut-2-ene, $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{C=CHCH}_3$.

**Apply the cis-trans test**

Cis-trans isomerism needs C=C with two different groups on each carbon. Pent-1-ene has $\text{CH}_2\text{=}$, so no. 2-methylbut-2-ene has $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{C=}$, so no. Only pent-2-ene from Y has $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ with two different groups at each end, so it exists as cis and trans forms. Therefore Y only gives the cis-trans pair.

options.A: Incorrect on oxidation. Z is tertiary, 2-methylbutan-2-ol, and does not react with mild oxidising agents. Only X and Y react, so X, Y and Z is wrong.
options.B: Wrong in both columns. Z does not oxidise, and Z dehydrates to (CH3)2C=CHCH3 which cannot show cis-trans isomerism because one C=C carbon carries two identical methyl groups.
options.C: Correct. X (primary) and Y (secondary) are oxidised but Z (tertiary) is not. Y dehydrates to pent-2-ene, CH3CH=CHCH2CH3, which exists as cis and trans isomers, while X gives pent-1-ene and Z gives 2-methylbut-2-ene, neither of which can show cis-trans isomerism.
options.D: Right about oxidation but wrong about dehydration. Z gives mainly 2-methylbut-2-ene which has two CH3 groups on one end of the double bond, so no cis-trans pair. It is Y that gives pent-2-ene with cis-trans isomerism.
